title: Pasting coherence for restriction of a module base-change square
statement: For schemes [def-pc-scheme] and module pullbacks and pushforwards [def-pc-module-pullback], fix commuting squares (f,f\prime,g,g\prime), (f,f_U,j_U,j_X), (f\prime,f_V\prime,j_V,j_X\prime), and (f_U,f_V\prime,g_V,g_V\prime), with j_V followed by g = g_V followed by j_U and j_X\prime followed by g\prime = g_V\prime followed by j_X. Define beta, rho, rho\prime and beta_V on modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] as mates of pushforwards of the top-map units under the chosen tensor-pullback adjunctions [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. Define c(k,l) as the inverse conjugate of pushforwardComp(k,l). For every F, define a=c(j_V,g).inv followed by bottom equality transport, c(g_V,j_U).hom and g_V^*rho_F; define b=rho\prime_{g\prime^*F} followed by f_V\prime pushforward of c(j_X\prime,g\prime).inv, top equality transport and c(g_V\prime,j_X).hom. Then j_V^*beta_F followed by b equals a followed by beta_V at j_X^*F. No openness or full inverse-image hypothesis is assumed.

proof.text: Apply the Mathlib inverse-mate and conjugate-equivalence whiskering identities to the private core equal to the displayed adjunction formula. After mateEquiv_hcomp, evaluate the right-adjoint squares on each module and open. Their sectionwise equality is directly Functor.map_comp, since the category of opens is thin. No separate scheme-specific pushforwardSquare_pasting theorem is declared or reproved; the general Mathlib functoriality theorem supplies this elementary step. The resulting identity gives horizontal pasting for the private core.
